results.name: Assisted Chin Up Reverse Wide Grip
instructions: Kneel on the platform pad of an assisted chin-up machine and grasp the handles with a reverse grip (palms facing you) positioned wider than shoulder-width apart.
Begin the movement by pulling your body upward until your chin is above the bar.
Slowly lower your body back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining proper form throughout the exercise.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your body and avoid flaring them out.
Use an appropriate level of assistance on the machine to ensure you can perform the exercise correctly.
Exhale as you pull your body upward and inhale as you lower it back down.
results.description: Assisted Chin Up Reverse Wide Grip is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with an assisted, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms.

results.name: Assisted Chin-Up on a Bench
instructions: Stand on a bench with your hands gripping a pull-up bar, palms facing towards you (supinated grip).
Use your legs to assist in pulling your body up towards the bar until your chin is above the bar.
Lower your body back down to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
Continue the movement in a controlled, rhythmic manner, using the bench for assistance.
tips: Focus on keeping your body aligned and avoid swinging to ensure proper form.
Use your legs for assistance, but focus on using your arms and back muscles to perform the pull-up.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull up and inhaling as you lower yourself down.
results.description: Assisted Chin-Up on a Bench is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

results.name: Assisted Close Grip Underhand Chin Up

results.name: Roman Chair Back Extension
instructions: Fix your feet to the footrests and press your thighs against the padded platform.
Place your arms across your chest and lean forward.
Raise yourself by leaning backward and forming an upright position.
Hold for a while, return to the initial position, and repeat.
tips: Keep your movements slow and controlled to maintain proper form and maximize muscle engagement.
Avoid hyperextending your back; stop when your body forms a straight line to prevent strain on your lower back.
Engage your core muscles throughout the exercise to support your spine and maintain stability.
results.description: Roman Chair Back Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.

results.name: Back Extension on Exercise Ball
instructions: Position your lower abdomen, face down on an exercise ball , with your feet planted firmly on the floor and your legs extended straight.
Place your hands lightly behind your head or cross them over your chest.
Bend at the waist to lower your upper body over the exercise ball, keeping your back straight.
Engage your lower back and glutes to lift your upper body back to the starting position, extending your back fully.
tips: Maintain a stable position by keeping your feet firmly planted on the floor.
Avoid rounding your back; keep it straight to ensure proper form and prevent injury.
Focus on engaging your lower back muscles to lift your torso, not your neck or arms.
results.description: Back Extension on Exercise Ball is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.
